source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which vitamin can be synthesized by the body when the skin is exposed to sunlight?
questions.rationale: Vitamins cannot be synthesized in the body except vitamin D, formed in the skin by UV exposure.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 13 Vitamins (PDF p. 331)
questions.quote: They cannot be synthesized (except vitamin D) in the body

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which group of vitamins can accumulate in the body and cause toxicity with excessive intake?
questions.rationale: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) are stored; water-soluble ones are readily excreted.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 13 Vitamins (PDF p. 331)
questions.quote: Fat soluble vitamins are stored in the body while water soluble vitamins are generally not stored in significant amounts and are readily excreted.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The main cause of preventable nutritional blindness in young children is lack of:
questions.rationale: Vitamin A is part of rhodopsin; deficiency ranges from night blindness to keratomalacia.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 13 Vitamin A (PDF p. 331)
questions.quote: Vitamin A deficiency is the main cause ofpreventable nutritional blindness among young children.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A child has difficulty seeing at dusk. This earliest sign of vitamin A deficiency is:
questions.rationale: Night blindness is the earliest functional sign; keratomalacia (softening of cornea) is the most severe.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 14 Vitamin A deficiency (PDF p. 344)
questions.quote: Nightblindness, a functional sign characterized by difficulty in seeing in dim light

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Foamy, cheesy patches on the temporal part of a child's conjunctiva are:
questions.rationale: Bitot's spots are a sign of vitamin A deficiency (xerophthalmia).
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 14 Vitamin A deficiency (PDF p. 344)
questions.quote: Bitot's spot — a cheesy, foamy deposit usually in the temporal quadrant of the eye

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: For prophylactic vitamin A supplementation, a 3-year-old child receives:
questions.rationale: Preventive doses: 100,000 IU for infants 6–11 months; 200,000 IU every 6 months for children 1–5 years.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 14 Vitamin A prevention (PDF p. 344)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: An 8-month-old infant receives which preventive vitamin A dose?
questions.rationale: Infants 6 months to under 1 year receive 100,000 IU.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 14 Vitamin A prevention (PDF p. 344)
questions.quote: Infants 6 months to < 1 year of age — 100,000 IU

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: To improve absorption of iron from malunggay and mongo, the mother should serve them with:
questions.rationale: Non-heme iron is poorly absorbed; vitamin C and meat enhance it, while tannins, phytates and oxalates inhibit it.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 13 Iron (PDF p. 333)
questions.quote: To improve absorption of non-heme iron, vitamin C-rich foods and meat should be eaten together with it.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which form of iron is best absorbed by the body?
options: Heme iron from meat and liver
questions.rationale: Heme iron (red meat, organ meats) is well absorbed; plant (non-heme) iron is poorly absorbed.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 13 Iron (PDF p. 333)
questions.quote: heme iron which is found in red meat, and organ meats (liver, spleen, kidney heart) and is well absorbed in the body.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which groups are most vulnerable to iron deficiency anemia?
questions.rationale: Vulnerable: infants, preschoolers, adolescent girls, pregnant and lactating women, the elderly.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 13 Iron (PDF p. 333)
questions.quote: the most vulnerable groups are infants, preschool children, adolescent girls, pregnant and lactating women and elderly.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Pallor from anemia should be checked at which body sites?
questions.rationale: Pallor is examined at the conjunctiva, inner lips, nail beds and palms.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 14 Iron deficiency anemia (PDF p. 343)
questions.quote: Pallor should be examined at three sites: conjunctiva, the inner lips and nail beds and palm of hands.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Besides poor diet, an important cause of iron deficiency anemia among Filipino children in rural areas is:
questions.rationale: Increased blood loss from hookworm, malaria and Trichuris contributes to iron deficiency.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 14 Iron deficiency anemia (PDF p. 343)
questions.quote: Inereased blood loss due to hookworm and malaria and to a limited extent trichuris

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A severely wasted child has an "old man's face," thin sparse hair and no edema, and still has a good appetite. This is:
questions.rationale: Marasmus is severe wasting from prolonged starvation; kwashiorkor shows pitting edema and moon face.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 14 Marasmus (PDF p. 342)
questions.quote: Marasmus results from prolonged starvation and is associated with severe wasting with classical signs of "old man's facie"

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A malnourished toddler has pitting edema of the legs, moon face, flaky-paint skin and alternating light bands in the hair. This is:
questions.rationale: Kwashiorkor: pitting edema, moon face, flag sign of hair and flaky paint dermatosis.
explanations: Not with these skin and hair signs.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 14 Kwashiorkor (PDF p. 342)
questions.quote: The main sign of kwashiorkor is the presence of pitting edema in the legs and feet

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: In the initial management of a child with severe acute malnutrition, the nurse watches especially for:
questions.rationale: Severely malnourished children risk hypoglycemia, hypothermia, dehydration, electrolyte imbalance and infection; stabilize first.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 14 Management of PEM (PDF p. 342)
questions.quote: Children with severe PEM are at risk of hypoglycemia, hypothermia, dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, micronutrient deficiencies and infection.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: A child's height-for-age is below −2 SD of the standard. This indicates:
questions.rationale: Low height-for-age reflects past, chronic undernutrition (stunting); low weight-for-height reflects wasting.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 13 Indices of nutritional status (PDF p. 339)
questions.quote: Height for age indicates past, chronic undernutlfion and a good index of stunting.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which index best detects a child who is currently wasted (thin for height)?
questions.rationale: Weight-for-height is a sensitive indicator of current nutritional status and distinguishes wasting from stunting.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 13 Indices of nutritional status (PDF p. 339)
questions.quote: Weight for height is a sensitive indicator of current nutritional status.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An adult weighs 72 kg and is 1.60 m tall. Her BMI is about 28. She is classified as:
questions.rationale: WHO adult BMI: <18.5 underweight; 18.5–24.9 normal; 25–29.9 overweight; ≥30 obese. 72 ÷ 2.56 ≈ 28.1.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 13 BMI classification (PDF p. 339)
questions.quote: BMI = Weight (kg)/ Height (m)2

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A mother is asked to recall all the foods her child ate in the past day. This dietary assessment method is the:
questions.rationale: In the 24-hour recall, the respondent recalls all foods eaten in the previous day; FFQ estimates usual long-term intake.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 13 Dietary methods (PDF p. 336)
questions.quote: Twenty-four hour food recall

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Iodine deficiency during pregnancy may cause which condition in the baby?
questions.rationale: Fetal iodine deficiency causes cretinism (mental and growth retardation, deaf-mutism).
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 14 Iodine deficiency (PDF p. 345)
questions.quote: Cretinism results when there is iodine deficiency during fetal life

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The national measure credited with dramatically reducing iodine deficiency among Filipino schoolchildren is:
questions.rationale: The Salt Iodization Law (ASIN Law, RA 8172) reduced the proportion of children with deficient urinary iodine.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 14 Iodine deficiency (PDF p. 345)
questions.quote: The implementation of the Salt Iodization Law in the Philippines can be regarded as instrumental

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Iodine status of a population is commonly assessed by measuring:
questions.rationale: Urinary iodine excretion among school-age children is a key biochemical indicator of IDD.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 14 Iodine deficiency (PDF p. 345)
questions.quote: Biochemical methods include determination of urinary iodine excretion among school age children

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Gums that bleed easily in a client who eats almost no fruits or vegetables suggest deficiency of:
questions.rationale: Bleeding gums are a suggestive clinical sign of vitamin C deficiency.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 13 Clinical signs (PDF p. 340)
questions.quote: Bleeding gums

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Where is about 99% of the body's calcium found?
questions.rationale: Calcium is the most abundant mineral; 99% is in bones and teeth, 1% in body fluids.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 13 Calcium (PDF p. 332)
questions.quote: Calcium is the most abundant mineral in the body with 99% found in bones and teeth
